name: pareto-two-objectives
description: Two-objective MAB with a concave part in its Pareto front (as in Drugan and Nowe, 2013), Gaussian noise 0.2, 20 runs. Regret of the 0.5 / 0.5 scalarization and Pareto measures.

notices.title: Default hyperparameters
notices.text: Paper values: alpha=1 for ParetoUCB1 and UCB1. Safe in theory, but they often explore too much.
notices.todo: Grid search: param_grid=True. Or set them, e.g. ParetoUCB1(alpha=0.1).

notices.title: Assumed constants
notices.text: Not given by the problem: b=1 (reward_range, ParetoUCB1 and UCB1).
notices.todo: Pass the true values to the policies.

notices.title: Not stored
notices.text: Pseudo-regret, reward per objective, per-action estimates, action of every step. The charts cannot show them.

notices.title: One point every 50 steps
notices.text: Between two stored points, the curve is drawn, not measured. You set log_interval=50.

notices.title: Slower timings
notices.text: Memory tracking (measure_memory=True) makes Python code about 5 times slower.
notices.todo: Compare CPU times only between runs with the same setting.

notices.title: Parallel runs
notices.text: Runs in parallel (n_jobs=4), one BLAS thread each.
notices.todo: Compare CPU times only between runs with the same n_jobs.
